samples.summary: revokeInvite's new `resolveId` step is never exercised with a slug — both new tests pass a UUID, so the slug→id branch is dead in the suite
samples.evidence: `revokeInvite` (workspace.service.ts:141) now calls `this.resolveId(workspaceId)` before the scoped `deleteMany`. Every revokeInvite test passes '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111', for which `resolveId` short-circuits on the UUID regex and never touches `prisma.workspace.findUnique`. So no test proves the deleteMany `where.workspaceId` is the *resolved* id when a slug is supplied (the mock `workspace.findUnique` would return `undefined` and throw NotFound — a failure mode nothing covers). The controller currently resolves first, so this is a latent gap rather than a live bug.

finding.summary: Non-owner test only counts "Remove member" buttons; it never checks the button is in the viewer's OWN row, so an inverted/wrong self-check still passes
finding.evidence: The new condition under test is `member.role !== "owner" && (isOwner || member.user.id === me?.id)` (workspace-settings.tsx:325-326). The test renders as MEMBER (id 2) with two non-owner members (ids 2 and 3) and asserts only `expect(screen.getAllByLabelText("Remove member")).toHaveLength(1)`. If the predicate were wrong in the opposite direction (e.g. `member.user.id !== me?.id`, rendering the trash button on OTHER_MEMBER's row instead of the viewer's), the count would still be exactly 1 and the test would stay green — i.e. the assertion is true regardless of which member the button belongs to. Asserting via the row (e.g. `within(screen.getByText("member").closest("tr"))`) is what would actually pin the behavior. Note the fixture has three members precisely to distinguish these cases, and the distinguishing assertion is the one that is missing.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the non-owner test asserts ONLY `expect(screen.getAllByLabelText("Remove member")).toHaveLength(1)` and never checks the button is in the viewer's own row. That is not the code in this repository. The test "hides them from a non-owner member" (workspace-settings.test.tsx:135-161) contains four assertions, and the row-anchored one the reviewer says is missing is present: line 140-144 does `waitFor(() => expect(within(memberRow(MEMBER.user.email)).getByLabelText("Remove member")).toBeTruthy())`, using the `memberRow` helper (lines 99-103) that resolves a specific `<tr>` via the unique email cell — literally the `within(...closest("tr"))` pattern the finding prescribes as the fix. Lines 148-152 and 153-155 further assert the button is ABSENT from OTHER_MEMBER's row and the OWNER's row. The finding's own counterexample does not survive: inverting the predicate at workspace-settings.tsx:325-326 to `member.user.id !== me?.id` would render the button on OTHER_MEMBER's row, keeping the count at 1, but would fail the waitFor at 140-144 (no button in MEMBER's row) and the queryByLabelText null-check at 148-152 (button present in OTHER_MEMBER's row). The test therefore goes red under the exact mutation claimed to leave it green. The owner test (110-133) makes the mirror per-row assertions, and a third test (163-178) clicks the button in MEMBER's own row and asserts removeMember was called with MEMBER.user.id, pinning member identity rather than merely that a mock fired. Grep for "Remove member" returns only this one test file plus the component, so no stale/shadowed copy is in play.
